free_tier.stated: No subscription and no perpetual free allowance: the entry plan is 'USD 0 / month - No subscription, top up from USD 5 - Unused credit rolls over, never expires', and new accounts start 'with USD 5 of signup credit'. Metering, quoted: 'vCPU ~USD 0.00041 / vCPU-min', 'Memory ~USD 0.0001 / GiB-min', 'Bandwidth USD 0.02 to USD 0.13 / GB'. Reserved boxes: 'Spark 1 | 0.25 vCPU | 0.5 GiB | USD 5/mo' through 'Core 8 | 8 vCPU | 16 GiB | USD 232/mo'.

chaining: prepaid credit that does not expire turns a monthly budget decision into a one-off one: USD 5 left in the wallet still runs a small app a year later, and the hourly meter means a job stopped promptly costs cents.

limits.value: the USD 5 credit is spent by the minute at about USD 0.0246 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.006 per GiB-hour, so it buys about 203 vCPU-hours and then the account pauses.

notes: Aggregator claim checked: free-for.dev says 'Free tier: the Starter plan runs everything on one instance in your own AWS account, no credit card needed (you pay AWS for the instance)'. That description is stale. The vendor now sells its own metered compute with a prepaid wallet, and the AWS bring-your-own-account arrangement is no longer on the site. The USD 5 signup credit is the only free capacity, and it is a one-off, not a monthly grant.
